definition_zh: 同化；吸收；使某物融入更大的整体
definition_en: the process of becoming like something else, or of absorbing something into a larger whole
core_image: 一颗石子落进一锅浓汤，外形渐渐消失，味道却散进整锅汤里
scene: 新搬来的家庭在几年里改说当地语言、参加本地节庆，孩子们的同学不再觉得他们外来。Over two generations, the immigrant family achieved full assimilation into the host community.
sceneCN: 这里 assimilation 指「移民群体逐步融入主流社会的文化同化」（第 1 个义项：群体吸收进主流文化的过程）；句意为经过两代人，这个移民家庭完成了对当地社会的同化。可辨识物件：街区、节庆旗帜、学校门口、家庭餐桌。

pos.zh: 同化；融合（社会文化义，常作不可数）
吸收（生理、认知或语音义）

forms.label: 可数复数（具体过程或案例）

derivatives.zh: 异化（语音或文化上的反向过程）

senses.title: Cultural absorption into a host society
senses.titleCN: 融入主流社会的文化同化
senses.definition: the process by which a group or person takes on the culture of a host society
senses.definitionCN: 群体或个人逐渐接受主流社会文化的过程
senses.example: Over two generations, the immigrant family achieved full assimilation into the host community.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两代人，这个移民家庭完成了对当地社会的同化。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to make like'; in society the process makes newcomers like the majority.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使相似」；在社会层面，这个过程使新来者变得像多数人。

senses.title: Physiological absorption
senses.definition: the process by which the body takes nutrients into its own tissue
senses.definitionCN: 身体把营养纳入自身组织的过程
senses.example: Assimilation of nutrients begins in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 营养的吸收从小肠开始。
senses.why: The body literally makes food like itself, turning foreign matter into tissue, which is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 身体确实把食物变得像自己，把外来物质变成组织，这是最古老的具体义。

senses.title: Cognitive assimilation
senses.definition: the fitting of new experience into an existing mental framework
senses.definitionCN: 把新经验纳入既有心智框架
senses.example: Piaget described assimilation as fitting new experience into an existing schema.
senses.exampleCN: 皮亚杰把同化描述为把新经验纳入既有图式。
senses.why: The mind, like the body, absorbs what is new by making it fit what is already there.
senses.whyCN: 心智与身体一样，通过让新事物贴合已有之物来吸收它。

senses.title: Phonetic assimilation
senses.definition: the change of a speech sound so that it becomes more like a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 一个语音变得与相邻语音更相似
senses.example: In handbag the n of hand becomes m by assimilation before b.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语复合词「手袋」中，前一词尾的鼻音受后接双唇音影响，经同化变成双唇鼻音。
senses.why: Sounds, like people, adjust to their neighbours; the technical sense applies the old verb to pronunciation.
senses.whyCN: 音与人一样会向邻居靠拢；这个技术义把古老的动词用到发音上。

senses.title: Immigrant assimilation policy
senses.definition: a state programme that expects newcomers to adopt the majority culture
senses.definitionCN: 要求新来者接受多数文化的国家政策
senses.example: The city's assimilation policy offered language classes but demanded cultural surrender.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的同化政策提供语言课程，却要求文化上的归顺。
senses.why: When the process is planned by institutions, the noun names a policy and carries its political weight.
senses.whyCN: 当过程由机构规划时，这个名词指一项政策，并带上政治分量。

senses.title: Structural assimilation
senses.definition: entry of a minority into the institutions and social networks of the majority
senses.definitionCN: 少数群体进入多数群体的制度与社会网络
senses.example: Structural assimilation meant immigrants entered clubs, schools and political parties.
senses.exampleCN: 结构性同化意味着移民进入俱乐部、学校与政党。
senses.why: Sociologists split assimilation into parts; the structural part concerns access to institutions rather than taste or language.
senses.whyCN: 社会学家把同化分成若干部分；结构部分关乎制度准入，而非口味或语言。

senses.title: Forced assimilation
senses.definition: assimilation imposed by power, often through schools, law or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 由权力强加的同化，常通过学校、法律或惩罚
senses.example: Boarding schools practised forced assimilation of indigenous children.
senses.exampleCN: 寄宿学校对原住民儿童实行强制同化。
senses.why: The same noun can name coercion, because absorption into a larger whole may be demanded rather than chosen.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能指强迫，因为融入更大整体可能是被要求而非自愿的。

senses.title: Abstract incorporation into a framework
senses.definition: the incorporation of a foreign element into an existing system or narrative
senses.definitionCN: 把外来要素并入既有体系或叙述
senses.example: The essay assimilates every dissent into one smooth narrative.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把一切异议都同化进一个平滑的叙述。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops people and bodies: any odd element can be made to fit a system.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义不再涉及人与身体：任何异质要素都可以被弄得贴合某个体系。

intro.en: Assimilation comes from Latin assimilatio, from assimilare 'to make like', built on ad- 'to' and similis 'like'. English uses it for bodies, minds, sounds and societies. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: assimilation 来自拉丁 assimilatio，源于 assimilare「使相似」，由 ad-「向」与 similis「相似」构成。英语用它指身体、心智、语音与社会。年代均为约数。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, similar'. It is generally connected with simul 'together' and similis 'like', but the pre-Latin shape is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: similis 意为「相似的」。一般认为它与 simul「一起」同源，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式，并无实际书证。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus similis produced assimilare 'to make like, to liken, to absorb'.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」加 similis 构成 assimilare「使相似、比作、吸收」。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century, first in the general sense of making one thing like another.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪进入英语，最初泛指使一物像另一物。

items.en: Physiology adopted it for the conversion of food into tissue, and psychology later for the fitting of new experience into existing schemas.
items.cn: 生理学用它指食物转化为组织，心理学后来用它指把新经验纳入既有图式。

items.en: Nineteenth-century sociology applied it to immigrant groups, and linguistics used it for sounds becoming like their neighbours.
items.cn: 十九世纪社会学把它用于移民群体，语言学则用它指语音向邻近语音靠拢。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link of similis to simul is generally accepted but the pre-Latin form is reconstructed, and the earliest use of each technical sense is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：similis 与 simul 的联系虽被一般接受，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式；各技术义的最早书证年代并不精确。

note.en: Group one is built on the same 'like' root; group two names absorption or blending under other names.
note.cn: 第一组同出「相似」词根；第二组是用其他名称表达吸收或混合的说法。

entries.definition: The action behind the noun; it can take a direct object or appear in the passive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动作；可带宾语，也可用被动式。

entries.definition: Describes a person or group already absorbed, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被吸收的个人或群体，而非过程。

entries.definition: Means tending to absorb or make similar; it describes a capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为有吸收或同化倾向的；描述一种能力。

entries.definition: The reverse process, in which sounds or traits become less alike; the prefix changes the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 相反的过程，语音或特质变得更不相似；前缀改变了方向。

entries.definition: Entry into a society without necessarily losing one's own culture; assimilation is stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 进入社会但未必失去自身文化；同化的程度更强。

entries.definition: The plain word for one thing taking in another, used of liquids, knowledge and groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指一物吸纳另一物的普通说法，可用于液体、知识与群体。

entries.definition: Cultural change through contact that can go both ways; assimilation usually points toward the majority.
entries.definitionCN: 接触引起的文化变化，可是双向的；同化通常指向多数群体。

entries.definition: The result of many things becoming the same; it stresses sameness rather than absorption.
entries.definitionCN: 指许多事物变得相同的结果，强调相同而非吸收。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real contrasts, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实对比，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ad- 'toward' plus similis 'like': to move toward being like.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 similis「相似」：朝「像」的方向移动。

normal.en: The family runs assimilate, assimilated, assimilation, assimilative, assimilable, assimilationist.
Fixed phrases: cultural assimilation, assimilation of immigrants, phonetic assimilation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：文化同化、移民的同化、语音同化。

normal.en: The same noun serves the stomach, the mind, the mouth and the state.
normal.cn: 同一个名词可用于胃、心智、口舌与国家。

normal.en: Opposite direction is marked by a different prefix in dissimilation.
normal.cn: 相反方向由 dissimilation 中的另一个前缀标记。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of sugar disappearing into hot tea.
abstract.cn: 想象一块糖消失在热茶里。

abstract.en: Picture a new word being spoken in the accent of its new street.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新词用它新所在街道的口音说出。

abstract.en: Picture a map redrawn until the old border is only a faint line.
abstract.cn: 想象地图被重画，旧边界只剩一道淡线。

examples.en: Assimilation into the village took a generation and cost the family its old language.
examples.cn: 融入这个村庄花了一代人的时间，也让这家人失去了旧语言。

examples.en: The laboratory measured the assimilation of iron in the digestive tract.
examples.cn: 实验室测量了消化道中铁的吸收。

examples.en: Linguists describe the assimilation of place of articulation in rapid speech.
examples.cn: 语言学家描述快速语流中发音部位的同化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」加「相似」加「过程」——朝「变得相似」走的过程

root: 拉丁 assimilare「使相似」= ad-（向）+ similis（相似），名词 assimilatio；similis 一般认为与 simul「一起」同源，但更早形态属重构。英语 assimilation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: something outside is made like the inside, whether the inside is a society, a body, a mind, a sound system or a written argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把外部之物变得像内部之物，这个「内部」可以是社会、身体、心智、语音系统或一篇论述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into thick soup, losing its outline while its taste spreads through the pot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子落进浓汤，外形渐失，味道却散进整锅。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND POLICY: a group may be absorbed by the majority, and the state may demand it.
branches.cn: 社会与政策：群体可能被多数吸收，国家也可能强制要求。

branches.en: BODY: food becomes tissue, the most concrete form of the process.
branches.cn: 身体：食物变成组织，这是该过程最具体的形式。

branches.en: MIND AND TEXT: new experience fits a schema, and an argument can absorb dissent.
branches.cn: 心智与文本：新经验贴合图式，一篇论述也能吸收异议。

branches.en: SOUND: a speech sound adjusts to its neighbour.
branches.cn: 语音：语音向邻近语音靠拢。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND FORCE: entry into schools and parties is different from compulsory absorption.
branches.cn: 制度与强制：进入学校与政党，不同于强迫吸收。

intro.en: Assimilation can be read from a Latin prefix, the Latin adjective for 'like', and the noun suffix that names a process.
intro.cn: assimilation 可以按拉丁前缀、表示「相似」的拉丁形容词，以及表示过程的名词后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis supplies similar, similarity and assimilate; ad- adds direction toward, and the noun suffix names the process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 similis 衍生 similar、similarity 与 assimilate；ad- 增添朝向，名词后缀指过程。

items.example: The prefix aims the action at a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向目标。

items.example: The adjective supplies the goal of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供动作的目标。

items.example: The verb names the act of making one thing like another.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指使一物像另一物。

items.meaning: the process of becoming like or being absorbed
items.example: Assimilation can be cultural or physical.
items.exampleCN: 同化可以是文化的，也可以是生理的。

items.example: An assimilated group speaks the majority language.
items.exampleCN: 被同化的群体说多数人的语言。

items.meaning: tending to absorb or make similar
items.example: The process is assimilative by nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程本质上是同化性的。

items.example: Some nutrients are more assimilable than others.
items.exampleCN: 有些营养比其他营养更易吸收。

items.example: The policy was defended by assimilationists.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策得到同化论者的辩护。

items.meaning: the reverse process, becoming less alike
items.exampleCN: 异化使相邻语音变得不同。

derivatives.meaning: to make unlike; to become less similar
